free_tier.stated: The free tier is static sites only: global CDN, 100 GB bandwidth, ~20s builds and unlimited sites at 0 EUR/mo, never billed and never drawing on the signup credit; plus S3-compatible object storage with 5 GB free and no egress fees. Every new account gets EUR 5 of credit valid for 90 days with no card check. Paid web services start at Nano (vCPU 0.1, RAM 256 MB, Disk 1 GB, Bandwidth 100 GB) at 3 EUR/mo and 0.0041 EUR/hr, then Starter (vCPU 0.5, RAM 512 MB, Disk 5 GB, Bandwidth 1 TB) at 5 EUR/mo and 0.0068 EUR/hr.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a machine, not an object
per_object_cap.notes: The primary constraint is the virtual machine hardware specification.

retention.stated: not applicable: the unit is a machine or an account, not stored bytes
retention.notes: a machine record: what is lost is the running process, not a stored object

notes: Aggregator claim checked: free-for.dev says 'European PaaS with automated deployments from GitHub for web services or static sites (1 web 0.1 vCPU/256 MB free), managed PostgreSQL and Valkey (30 days for free), Transactional Email (3,000 emails/month free), S3 compatible storage (5 GB/free)'. The free web service is wrong: the vendor table marks Static Sites as the 0 EUR row and prices the 0.1 vCPU web service at EUR 3 a month, so a reader would build against a free tier that does not exist. The 5 GB of object storage is real. The 30-day free database was not confirmed: the managed PostgreSQL rows on the same table start at EUR 3.
